7 Best App Development Agencies (2026): Pricing, Ratings, and Fit

"App development agency" gets typed into Google by a founder who wants a $15,000 MVP and a hospital system that needs a $400,000 HIPAA-compliant patient portal, and both get served the same search results. The gap between those two builds isn't a matter of degree, it's a different kind of agency entirely. This guide compares 7 real app development agencies on verified reviews, pricing, and what each one is actually built for, so you can tell which shape you need before the first sales call.

Disclosure: ManasFlow publishes this list and ranks itself first. Every other agency was scored on the same rubric below, and every Clutch figure cited, including ours, was cross-checked live on September 5, 2026 (ArcTouch added and verified September 8, 2026).
How we ranked these agencies

Four criteria: (1) Verified reputation: real Clutch reviews, not a curated case-study page. (2) Pricing transparency: a published minimum project size and rate band. (3) Build type clarity: does the agency state plainly whether it builds MVPs, polished consumer apps, or vertical-specific enterprise apps, or does that only surface after a discovery call? (4) Specialization depth: a real, checkable focus (a vertical, a build philosophy, a price tier) rather than a generalist "we build any app" pitch.

1. ManasFlow, best for AI-native app builds with a fixed 30-day sprint

ManasFlow builds a live app in a fixed 30-day sprint, architecture, integrations, and QA included, with one senior engineer directing a fleet of AI agents to cover what a larger team would need. That's a written delivery window, not a range.

Why we rank ManasFlow #1: a specific, contractual timeline most agencies on this list scope per engagement instead of committing to in writing. The same model extends past launch into AI agent development and custom workflow automation, so the app doesn't get handed to a different team the moment it ships.

What we will not claim: a large public review count. ManasFlow's Clutch profile carries 3 verified reviews at 5.0/5 as of September 2026, the smallest count on this list, disclosed with the same evidence bar every other entry is held to.
Best for: founders and teams that want a specific, written delivery date for a first version, and continuity into AI features and automation rather than a design-only handoff.
Pricing: the 30-day MVP development sprint is fixed-price and scoped on a free 30-minute call; embedded engineers start at $60,000 a year.
Pros: fixed delivery window in writing; AI agent and automation capability most app-only agencies on this list don't offer natively.
Cons: smallest public review count on this list; not built for teams that specifically want a large in-house-style design team.
2. Wve Labs, best for accessible mid-tier builds with a large review base
Wve Labs has the largest verified Clutch review count on this list at 111 reviews, rated 4.9/5, with a minimum project size around $10,000.
Best for: teams that want a solid, mid-tier build without the premium design-agency price tag, backed by a large enough review sample to trust the rating.
Pricing: $25-49/hr, $10,000+ minimum project size.
Pros: largest independently verified review count on this list; accessible entry point relative to the premium agencies here.
Cons: less specialized than the vertical-specific agencies on this list (healthcare, social-impact); generalist positioning.
3. Lickability, best for premium, design-led native app builds

Lickability positions itself at the premium end of native app development, with the agency's own site stating a fully-featured, polished app typically runs $100K+, and smaller, tighter-scope projects landing in the $50K-$100K range. Clutch shows 31 verified reviews at a perfect 5.0/5.
Best for: consumer-facing apps where design and native-platform polish materially affect adoption, and budget supports a premium build.
Pricing: $200-300/hr, $25,000+ minimum project size, the highest rate band on this list.
Pros: perfect Clutch rating; design-forward positioning backed by the agency's own transparent, published cost ranges rather than a vague "contact us."
Cons: highest hourly rate on this list by a wide margin; overkill for a simple MVP that just needs to validate demand.
4. Saritasa, best for custom software plus immersive tech alongside the app

Saritasa is a full-service custom software and immersive-technology firm, not an app-only shop, with capability spanning fintech, healthcare, manufacturing, logistics, media, IoT, and AR/VR. Clutch shows 106 verified reviews at 4.8/5, with quality specifically rated 4.9 and willingness-to-refer at 4.9.
Best for: builds where the mobile or web app is one piece of a larger custom software or AR/VR system, not a standalone product.
Pricing: $100-149/hr, $50,000+ minimum project size.
Pros: broad technical range (AR/VR, IoT) most pure app shops don't cover; consistently high quality and referral scores across a large review sample.
Cons: enterprise-tier minimum prices out early-stage founders who need a simple MVP; broader scope than a team that wants an app-only specialist.
5. 3 Sided Cube, best for social-impact and mission-driven apps

3 Sided Cube builds apps with an explicit social-impact orientation, delivering discovery, design, build, test, launch, and long-term support as one team on every project. Clutch shows 47 verified reviews at 4.9/5.

Best for: nonprofits, public-sector, and mission-driven organizations that want a partner with a demonstrated track record in social-impact app work specifically, not a generalist agency that happens to accept the project.
Pricing: $100-149/hr, $50,000+ minimum project size, with project investments reported up to roughly £500,000 for larger engagements.
Pros: genuine, checkable specialization in social-impact work rather than a claimed value-add; full-team continuity from discovery through long-term support.
Cons: enterprise-tier minimum project size rules this out for smaller mission-driven organizations with limited budgets.
6. MindSea, best for healthcare-specific app development

MindSea is a healthcare app development company founded in 2007, based in Halifax, Nova Scotia, building custom mobile and web applications specifically for healthcare organizations across the US and Canada. Clutch shows roughly 41 verified reviews at a perfect 5.0/5.
Best for: healthcare organizations that need an app partner with real, focused experience in the vertical, not a generalist agency treating healthcare as one industry among many.
Pricing: project costs from $10,000 to over $1 million depending on scope; no fixed minimum published, scoped per engagement.
Pros: genuine, nearly two-decade specialization in healthcare specifically; perfect Clutch rating across a real review sample.
Cons: narrower vertical focus is a mismatch for teams outside healthcare; wide pricing range makes early budgeting harder without a direct conversation.
7. ArcTouch, best for enterprise-scale, cross-vertical native apps

ArcTouch is a native app development agency with a diversified client base spanning consumer products and services, financial services, medical, hospitality and leisure, retail, and supply chain and logistics, rather than a single-vertical specialist. On a Clutch-featured case study, Midtown Athletic Clubs' VP of Marketing is quoted saying the team was "flexible and always attentive to the project's needs," on an engagement valued between $1M and $9.9M that reached 65% member app penetration within 90 days of launch. Clutch shows 37 verified reviews at 4.9/5.

Best for: enterprises that need a proven native-app partner across several possible industries at once, rather than a narrow vertical specialist, and whose budget supports the highest minimum on this list.
Pricing: $50-99/hr, $100,000+ minimum project size, the highest minimum on this list by a wide margin.

Pros: real, checkable outcome data cited directly in client reviews (specific adoption percentages, not just satisfaction scores); genuine breadth across multiple industries rather than a single narrow niche.

Cons: the $100,000+ minimum rules this out for any MVP-stage or budget-constrained build; broad cross-vertical positioning is a weaker fit than MindSea or 3 Sided Cube for a team that specifically wants deep, narrow vertical expertise.

Red flags when evaluating an app development agency
A portfolio full of polished screenshots with no mention of backend architecture, data model, or what happens when the app needs to scale past the demo.
No published minimum project size or rate anywhere, forcing a sales call before any number is shared, not even a wide range.
A "we build any kind of app" pitch with no real specialization behind it. The agencies with the strongest track records on this list all have a specific, checkable focus.
No clear answer on who owns the codebase and app-store accounts after launch. You should own both outright.
A quoted timeline with no accountability if it slips. Ask what happens contractually if the delivery date is missed.
How to choose the right app development agency
1) Is this an MVP to validate demand, or a polished consumer product?

If you need a specific, written delivery date to test a concept, ManasFlow's 30-day sprint is built for that. If design polish and native-platform feel are the priority and budget supports it, Lickability's premium positioning fits.
2) Does your build have a specific vertical or technical requirement?
Healthcare-specific: MindSea. Social-impact or nonprofit: 3 Sided Cube. AR/VR or IoT alongside the app: Saritasa.
3) What's your realistic budget?

Wve Labs starts around $10,000. Lickability and ManasFlow scope per project without a hard published floor for the sprint model. Saritasa and 3 Sided Cube start around $50,000. MindSea's range runs from $10,000 to $1 million depending on scope. ArcTouch is the highest floor on this list at $100,000+.
4) Do you need AI features or automation built into the app itself?

If the app needs AI agents, RAG-grounded features, or backend automation as a core part of the product rather than an add-on, ManasFlow is built around that natively; several agencies on this list would treat it as a separate, unscoped conversation.

FAQ
What does an app development agency do?

An app development agency designs, builds, and launches mobile or web apps for clients, and usually maintains them after launch. The work covers product scoping, UX and UI design, front-end and back-end engineering, App Store and Play Store submission, and ongoing updates. Agencies differ mainly in the build type they are set up for: fixed-timeline MVPs, premium design-led apps, or regulated enterprise builds.
How much does it cost to hire an app development agency?

Costs on this list range from around $10,000 (Wve Labs) to $500,000+ for larger engagements (3 Sided Cube, Saritasa). ManasFlow's 30-day sprint and MindSea's healthcare builds are both scoped per project rather than a flat rate card. Budget $25,000-$100,000 as a realistic range for a real MVP with more than a handful of screens.
What is the difference between an app development agency and a software development agency?

In practice, the terms overlap heavily. "App development agency" usually implies the deliverable is a mobile or web application specifically, while "software development agency" can include backend systems, internal tools, or infrastructure with no consumer-facing app at all. Several agencies, including ManasFlow and Saritasa, cover both under one engagement.
Should I hire a generalist app agency or a vertical specialist?

If your app has real domain-specific requirements, healthcare compliance, social-impact reporting, regulated data, a specialist with a genuine track record in that vertical (MindSea for healthcare, 3 Sided Cube for social impact) reduces real risk. A generalist agency is a reasonable fit for a standard consumer or B2B app with no specific regulatory or domain complexity.
How do I evaluate an app agency's Clutch reviews?

Check review count alongside star rating, not instead of it. A perfect 5.0/5 across 3 reviews (ManasFlow) is a smaller sample than a 4.9/5 across 111 reviews (Wve Labs). Read a handful of the actual reviews for specifics rather than trusting the aggregate score alone.
Can an app development agency build AI features into the app?

Some can as an add-on; fewer build it in as a core capability. ManasFlow specifically engineers AI agent and automation features as part of the same build rather than as a bolt-on requiring a second vendor. Ask any agency directly what AI capability they've actually shipped, not just discussed.
What should I ask before signing with an app development agency?

Ask for a specific delivery date in the contract, not a range. Ask who owns the codebase, app-store accounts, and any third-party API keys after handoff. Ask for a past app that's still live and maintained today, not just a portfolio screenshot. If your build has a specific vertical requirement, ask for a named, checkable example in that exact space.
The build type matters more than the badge

Every agency on this list can ship a working app. What actually differentiates them is the build type they're set up for, a fixed-timeline MVP, a premium design-led product, an enterprise vertical build, and matching that to your actual need before comparing star ratings is the real decision.
